Thought: I need to analyze each statement about sodium fluoride to determine which ones are true.

A. In case of poisoning, barium chloride serves as an antidote - I need to check if barium chloride is used as an antidote for sodium fluoride poisoning. This doesn't sound correct, as barium compounds themselves are toxic.

B. It causes burns to the gastrointestinal mucosa - Sodium fluoride is corrosive in high concentrations, but I need to verify if it specifically causes burns to the gastrointestinal mucosa.

C. It has a narcotic effect on the central nervous system (CNS) - I need to check if sodium fluoride has narcotic effects on the CNS. This doesn't sound like a property of sodium fluoride.

D. It is used for caries prophylaxis - This is definitely true. Sodium fluoride is commonly used in toothpastes, mouthwashes, and water fluoridation to prevent dental caries (cavities).

Let me analyze each option more carefully:

A. Barium chloride is not an antidote for sodium fluoride poisoning. In fact, calcium compounds (like calcium gluconate) are used to treat fluoride poisoning by binding with fluoride ions. This statement is false.

B. In high concentrations, sodium fluoride can be corrosive and irritating to tissues, including the gastrointestinal mucosa. Ingestion of concentrated sodium fluoride can cause gastric irritation and damage. This statement appears to be true.

D. Sodium fluoride is definitely used for caries prophylaxis (prevention of dental cavities). This is one of its most common applications in dentistry and public health. This statement is true.

C. Sodium fluoride does not have narcotic effects on the CNS. Fluoride toxicity can affect the nervous system, but not as a narcotic. This statement is false.

Based on my analysis, options B and D appear to be correct.
